outcome: successful labor (vaginal delivery of both fetuses)
failed labor (cesarean delivery of one or two fetuses)
cohort: 519 cases of twin pregnancies that underwent labor in a single hospital between July 2016 and June 2023.
finding: Advanced maternal age, high pre-delivery BMI, and vertex/transverse fetal presentation were identified as risk factors for failed vaginal labor in twin pregnancies, while multiparity, previous premature birth, and neuraxial analgesia were protective factors.
mod_finding: The study identified several factors (maternal age, BMI, fetal presentation, parity, previous premature birth, and neuraxial analgesia) that significantly influenced the success of vaginal delivery in twin pregnancies.
